summary: Corporate campaigns for farmed animals in Latin America and Southeast Asia: cage-free egg commitments, pig welfare commitments in Brazil, and replacing meat in institutional meals. A re-implementation of Animal Charity Evaluators' cost-effectiveness sheet for its 2025 recommendation, covering three programs (about 84% of programme spending). It is more than ten times its peers because its cage-free commitments cover about 20.7 million hens a year in Latin America, 7.9 million credited to Sinergia, for about $0.9 million of campaign spending: some 31 hen-years out of cages per dollar before compliance, each counting the shared 17.5 SADs.

sections.title: Cage-free campaigns
sections.explainer: Commitments by 39 food companies to stop buying eggs from caged hens. Benefits last as long as commitments are honoured, discounted for other groups' share of the credit and for companies that renege.

sections.title: Institutional meat reduction
sections.explainer: Nourishing Tomorrow: schools and other institutions in Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia replacing some meat meals. ACE assumes each commitment lasts a single year, likely an underestimate.

sections.title: Pig welfare campaigns
sections.explainer: Commitments by 10 Brazilian pork producers to end gestation crates and some piglet mutilations.

sections.title: Costs
sections.explainer: Each program's annual spending, scaled up by ACE to Sinergia's newer total budget.

sections.title: Bottom line
sections.explainer: Suffering averted per dollar across the three modelled programs. The remaining ~16% of programme spending (work with financial institutions) is unmodelled, not assumed to be zero or equal.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: charityevals adjustments on top of ACE's model.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model, not ACE's. Ambitious Impact's suffering-adjusted days (SADs) count each species' pain as a share of a person's, using its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' estimates go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the one animal slider, under Your values.

rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: how many years a won commitment counts before it would have come anyway reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (5 by default), like every model that credits a won reform. ACE's own figure, Rethink Priorities' 15 years (4–36) for how long the policy changes until it would have happened anyway, is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view.

rows.label: Years from winning the commitments until they take effect
rows.explainer: Ours, not ACE's. The commitments were won in 2023; the deadlines ACE lists run from 2025 to 2030 (most hens are at companies with no deadline listed), so the hens' lives change some years later. Our judgment: 4 years, 2 to 7. ACE counts the benefit from the year the commitment is won; the evaluator view keeps that.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the commitments take effect
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: every model discounts the wait until a won reform takes effect at "Next year's good counts less by", as climate models discount the wait until tonnes are avoided. ACE counts the hens from the year of the win, so the evaluator view uses 1.

rows.label: Hen-years over the whole period (discounted)
Share of companies that keep their commitment
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: the share of cage-free commitments companies keep reads the shared figure (facts: sad_factors.commitment_fulfilment_cage_free, 92% of commitments due by 2024 fulfilled, Chicken Watch), as every model crediting a cage-free pledge does. ACE's own 53% (the midpoint of 22 of 58 companies in one tracker and 113 of 164 in another) is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view.

rows.explainer: Across 25 institutions, as reported by Sinergia. Context: the SADs row below is ACE's conversion of these meals.

rows.label: SADs averted by meals replaced
rows.explainer:
Fewer animals raised for the replaced meals, times the suffering in each animal's life. ACE calls the SADs-per-meal figures rough.

ACE's estimate, 900,203 SADs (86,972 to 1,713,434) for 997,510 meals, is the source of the shared figure for a replaced meal (Suffering-adjusted days per animal, under Data). Our view multiplies the meals by that shared figure, so a replaced meal counts the same in every model; the evaluator view keeps ACE's total.

rows.label: SADs a year from commitments due in 2023, before sharing credit
rows.explainer: Sows and piglets a year covered by each producer's commitment, times ACE's SADs per animal for the improvement, summed over the producers whose transition deadline is 2023 (Aurora, BRF, JBS, Master Agroindustrial, Pif Paf): 37.95M. Reproduces ACE's sheet: each producer's all-years total is this times its years brought forward, discounted at 4%.

rows.label: Years the pig commitments count before they would have come anyway
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (5 by default), like every model that credits a won reform. ACE counts each producer's years until Brazil's legal deadline (1 to 22 years; 9.47 is the single span that gives ACE's total), kept as the evaluator's.

rows.label: SADs from all commitments, all years, before sharing credit
rows.explainer: SADs from all the pig commitments, all years counted, before sharing credit. Changed for consistency: ACE counts each producer from its transition deadline to Brazil's legal deadline (1 to 22 years) and doesn't discount the wait until the deadline; ours counts the shared years for every producer, from its deadline, with the wait discounted at "Next year's good counts less by". ACE's total, 713.8M, is the evaluator's (ACE's sheet lists each producer's SADs after sharing credit; dividing by Sinergia's share gives it). The per-animal SADs are ACE's 2024 ones ('SADs per animal' tab): 84.55 and 51.75 for sows in crates and crate-free, 34.85 and 20.18 for piglets with and without mutilations; the group-housing and single-mutilation figures are older SAD values times 3.18, Ambitious Impact's stand-in for pain intensity growing exponentially between categories (ACE's Aquatic Life Institute sheet, 'SADs Estimate'!B16 comment). It scales pain, not species: Ambitious Impact's 2024 pig weight is applied separately, and divided out in ced_pig.

rows.explainer: Campaigning is mostly people: researchers, campaigners and corporate negotiators. Advocacy nonprofits typically spend well over half their budget on staff. We haven't seen Sinergia's own breakdown, so this is a guess. Range is ours.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give
Fall in production per meal not eaten
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: when fewer meals with meat are eaten, prices fall and others eat a little more, so production falls by less (0.76 per unit for chicken, Norwood and Lusk; facts: sad_factors.production_response). Every diet-change model multiplies the suffering of meals replaced by it, as charityevals' own diet template does. ACE counts one meal less eaten as one meal less produced (1), kept in the evaluator view. Applies to the meals replaced only, not to the welfare commitments.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: SADs averted for chickens per dollar you give: cage-free hens count as chickens, the pig campaigns as pigs, and replaced meals by ACE's global estimate of which animals a meal spares (Share of a replaced meal's suffering, under Data). A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row marginal_vs_past_average).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: The SADs for chickens with the hen weight built into the 2024 SADs ACE used (46% of a person's) taken out, which leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 here by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weight, so ACE's own result reproduces.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give: pigs
rows.explainer: SADs averted for pigs per dollar you give: cage-free hens count as chickens, the pig campaigns as pigs, and replaced meals by ACE's global estimate of which animals a meal spares (Share of a replaced meal's suffering, under Data). A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row marginal_vs_past_average).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: pigs
rows.explainer: The SADs for pigs with the pig weight built into the 2024 SADs ACE used (63% of a person's) taken out, and Rethink Priorities' estimate of how much pigs can suffer relative to a chicken put in. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weights, so ACE's own result reproduces.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar you give: fish
rows.explainer: SADs averted for fish per dollar you give: cage-free hens count as chickens, the pig campaigns as pigs, and replaced meals by ACE's global estimate of which animals a meal spares (Share of a replaced meal's suffering, under Data). A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row marginal_vs_past_average).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: fish
rows.explainer: The SADs for fish with the fish weight built into the 2024 SADs ACE used (about 27% of a person's) taken out, and Rethink Priorities' estimate of how much fish can suffer relative to a chicken put in. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weights, so ACE's own result reproduces. The fish weight is a stand-in, our judgment: Rethink Priorities estimated only carp and salmon, and their mean stands for every farmed and wild-caught fish (facts: welfare_ranges.fish_vs_chicken, kind judgment).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, all species, counted as a chicken's. The headline converts this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain.
